publication.subtitle: The global today cards
publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Teacher, Bystander Stop School Shooter, Killing Attacker
cards.content: An Oregon teacher, attempting to stop a 16-year-old student who opened fire on a special education class, was aided by a bystander who shot and killed the student. The bystander, identified by the student's family as Kaylub Giamanco, had been driving by the school when he saw the student firing. He quickly grabbed his own .40-caliber pistol and intervened, firing multiple times and stopping the student. The attack left three children and a teacher dead, and two others injured. Police credited the teacher's and Giamanco's actions with saving lives.

cards.title: Unprecedented protests erupt in Albania's major cities
cards.content: Albania has seen unprecedented protests with clashes between protesters and anti-riot police in major cities. The protests started as a student movement demanding education fee and cost of living reforms, but escalated into violent scenes with stone-throwing, water cannon, and tear gas. The government has accused opposition leader Sali Berisha of instigating chaos, while protesters say they are seeking justice for corruption allegations against ministers. The violence has spread to several cities, and the government has warned that it tarnishes Albania's image and affects its European path.

cards.title: Pastor and wife charged with kidnapping in South Africa
cards.content: A pastor and his wife in South Africa were arrested and charged with kidnapping after authorities found over 200 people, some in chains, being held at an illegal rehabilitation center in Mpumalanga province. The facility had grossly inhumane conditions, with patients found with sores and others chained together. The couple is expected to appear in court on Monday.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Losing Species Hurts Ecosystem Benefits, Study Reveals
cards.content: Scientists have found that losing species can have a significant impact on the benefits that ecosystems provide, such as pollination, clean water, and carbon storage. The largest global study of its kind combined data from over 400 studies and found that as biodiversity rises, these benefits also increase. The study suggests that ecosystems have less spare capacity than previously thought, and that species losses can have a cumulative effect on the benefits they provide. The research also found that some ecosystem services, such as marine carbon sequestration, are more sensitive to biodiversity than others.

cards.title: 120-million-year-old meat-eating dinosaur species found in Britain
cards.content: A 120-million-year-old dinosaur fossil, previously unknown and unnoticed for nearly a century, has been identified as a new species of meat-eating dinosaur called Invictibellatrix amberina. The dinosaur, roughly the size of a large tiger, lived in what is now Britain and was a member of the megaraptoran group, which was previously unknown in Europe. The discovery was made by a research team led by University College London using a fossil originally found on the Isle of Wight. The team used computed tomography to examine the fossil and compared it to other carnivorous dinosaurs to confirm its identity.

cards.title: US scientists discover more efficient nuclear fusion process
cards.content: Scientists at the US Department of Energy's Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory have discovered a potentially more efficient way to achieve nuclear fusion, the process that powers the Sun. By changing the order in which plasma is heated and compressed, researchers found that dramatically less energy is needed to reach ignition, a crucial milestone in the pursuit of practical fusion power. The new approach could lead to better designs and operations for fusion machines, which are being developed to generate electricity for the power grid.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Sardinian Village Has High Rate of Centenarian Women
cards.content: A Sardinian village, Bolotana, has an unusually high number of centenarians, with women having an exceptional pattern of survival after age 70. Researchers found that women in Bolotana have a 13.8% chance of living to 100, compared to 3.5% in Italy and 3.6% in the US. The village's historical records, dating back centuries, allowed the researchers to independently verify ages and reconstruct residents' life histories.

cards.title: Medication Reduces Inflammation, Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes Patients
cards.content: Researchers found that a diabetes medication, empagliflozin, changes how certain immune cells behave in the bloodstream, potentially reducing harmful inflammation and cardiovascular risk. In a small human clinical trial, the medication reduced inflammatory cell clusters after just two weeks, with measurable effects. The study, published in the American Heart Association journal Circulation, provides the first direct evidence that this medication can alter specific immune cells in humans.

cards.title: Fat Before Carbs Regulates Blood Sugar in Mice Study
cards.content: In a breakthrough study, researchers found that eating fat before carbohydrates can help regulate blood sugar levels by slowing down stomach emptying and reducing the initial spike. This effect was observed in mice and may be applicable to humans, offering a potential dietary strategy to manage post-meal blood sugar rises, an important treatment target in diabetes.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Global Deforestation Drops 15%, Still Off Track to Meet Goal
cards.content: Global deforestation declined by 15% in 2025 to seven million hectares, but the world remains off track to meet its goal of halting deforestation by 2030. Although the decline is the sharpest since the 2018-2020 baseline, a 10.7 million hectare deforestation reduction shortfall has accumulated since 2021, and only 17.33% of the world's land and inland waters are protected.

cards.title: NASA Astronaut Shows Ancient Moon Rock Formation in Madagascar
cards.content: A NASA astronaut took a photo from the International Space Station that shows a 600-million-year-old rock formation in Madagascar, which shares a surprising connection with the Moon. The rock, anorthosite, is found on the Moon's surface and in a few places on Earth, including Madagascar, where it forms a distinctive circular feature that stands out in photographs taken from space.

cards.title: Floating solar farms expand renewable energy production
cards.content: Floating solar installations are becoming an increasingly attractive option for regions where land is limited. Panels installed on reservoirs and other water bodies can generate electricity while reducing pressure on valuable land resources.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Global film festivals spotlight a new generation of filmmakers
cards.content: Film festivals around the world are giving greater attention to emerging directors and independent productions. Organisers say new filmmakers are experimenting with storytelling techniques and technologies while exploring social and cultural themes.

cards.title: New stadium technology changes how fans experience live sports
cards.content: Sports venues are adopting larger digital displays, real-time statistics and connected services to create more interactive experiences for spectators. The technology is also helping teams analyse matches and improve stadium operations.

cards.title: Music platforms experiment with new ways for artists to reach audiences
cards.content: Music platforms are experimenting with new discovery tools, personalised recommendations and direct connections between artists and listeners. The changes are reshaping how new musicians build audiences and release their work.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: US-Iran tensions: Record 12 ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz
cards.content: A record 12 ships reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz between October 5 and 11, with 6 vessels struck on Sunday alone, the largest weekly number since the US-Israeli war with Iran began. The attacks have slowed the recovery in oil shipments through the strait, with industry data suggesting a decrease in shipments. The US military says commercial traffic continues to flow through the strait with coordinated protection from US forces and regional partners.

cards.title: UK Chancellor Plans Tax Hike on Banks to Boost Revenue
cards.content: UK Chancellor John Healey is planning to increase taxes on the bank sector, with possible options including reversing a 2023 reduction in the bank surcharge or raising the bank levy. Bank shares fell on expectations of a tax hike, with Lloyds and NatWest dropping over 2%. Some experts argue that banks, which made £15bn in profit in the first half of the year, should contribute more to the government's budget. Healey praised the role banks play in the UK economy, but trade unions and some experts call for a fairer share of taxes from the sector.

cards.title: Small businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence tools
cards.content: Small businesses are adopting AI tools for customer support, marketing, document processing and data analysis. Lower-cost AI services are making technologies that were previously available mainly to large companies more accessible to smaller firms.
